claims.text: Language models are highly sensitive to epistemic markers in prompts, with accuracies varying more than 80%.
Expressions of high certainty in prompts result in a 7% decrease in accuracy compared to low certainty expressions.
Factive verbs hurt language model performance.
Markers of uncertainty are associated with answers on question-answering websites in a popular pretraining dataset.
Markers of certainty are associated with questions on question-answering websites in a popular pretraining dataset.

evidence.description: Accuracies varying more than 80% when injecting epistemic markers into QA prompts.
High certainty expressions led to a 7% decrease in accuracy compared to low certainty expressions.
Evaluation shows factive verbs consistently hurt performance.
Evaluation shows evidentials consistently benefit performance.
Pretraining dataset analysis links uncertainty markers to answers.
Pretraining dataset analysis links certainty markers to questions.

methodologies.name: Epistemic Marker Prompt Injection Analysis
methodologies.description: Injecting 50 typology-derived epistemic markers into question-answering prompts and measuring impact on language model accuracy alongside pretraining corpus association analysis.

limitations.text: LM behavior may reflect mimicking observed language use rather than truly reflecting epistemic uncertainty.
